criteria.semantics: A native <a href> whose text is the link's label: it goes somewhere (another page or another place on this one), it never does something (that is a button).

keyboard.outcome: Focus moves to the link and is strongly visually indicated.
Follows the link: the browser goes to its href.

criteria.name: The link's label, the same words as its visible text; its purpose is clear from them alone.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the link's label grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the link reflow with its text, whole and with no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native <a> element.
The link goes where the model says: its href is the link's href.
WHEN I use the Tab key I SEE focus reach the link: it has an href and no negative tabindex.
WHEN the link has focus I SEE a focus ring of at least 2px in the focus color.
The link's text is its label, so its accessible name matches what I see.
WHEN I Tab to the link with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR its purpose is clear and I HEAR it identify itself as a link.
WHEN I swipe to the link with a mobile screen reader (TalkBack, VoiceOver) I HEAR its name and its role of link, and a double tap follows it.
WHEN I press Enter on the link I HEAR the browser go somewhere: the new page's title, or the place on this page.

criteria.semantics: One focusable control in the window's tab order: its label in the accent color, underlined and ringed in the focus color while focused. A /page/{name} link loads that screen through the host's kernel; an http(s) or mail link opens in the system handler. Once GPUI exposes a tree: an AccessKit Link node named by its label, its URL as the node's URL, with a Click action that follows it (AXLink on macOS, the Hyperlink control type with the Invoke pattern on Windows, a link with the Hyperlink interface on AT-SPI).

keyboard.outcome: Focus moves to the link, in reading order, and the focus ring and underline show.
Focus moves back to the control before it, wrapping to the last.
Follows the link (Return on macOS): the window loads the screen it names, opens an http(s) or mail link in the system handler, or says in words why it cannot.

criteria.name: The link's label, the same words as its visible text.
criteria.role: Link (VoiceOver: link; Narrator: link; Orca: link).

setting.statement: WHEN I set the system text size to 200% (Windows' Accessibility, Text size; GNOME's Large Text or text scaling factor) I SEE the link's label grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I raise the display scale (macOS' Displays, Larger Text; Windows' Scale at 150% or 200%; GNOME's Scale at 200%) I SEE the link's label drawn sharp and larger, whole and without overlapping.

WHEN I turn on the platform's high contrast (macOS' Increase contrast, a Windows contrast theme, the desktop portal's contrast) I SEE the window switch to the high-contrast palette by itself, the link's label at 7:1.
WHEN I choose the high-contrast theme for the window I SEE the link's label and its focus ring drawn in the high-contrast palette, every pair at 7:1.
WHEN I magnify the screen (macOS Zoom, Windows Magnifier, GNOME's Zoom) with focus following I SEE the magnifier follow the keyboard focus to the link's label.

check.statement: WHEN the window opens or loads a screen I SEE it hold the keyboard focus, so Tab reaches the link without a click.
The link is one stop in the window's tab order, and focusing it puts the keyboard focus there.

WHEN I use Tab and Shift+Tab I SEE focus reach the link in reading order, top to bottom, wrapping at either end, on every platform (macOS' Keyboard navigation setting does not change it: the window keeps its own tab order).
WHEN the link has focus I SEE a 2px ring in the focus color drawn outside it, on the window's ground, a pair the palettes hold to 3:1.
WHEN I press Enter on the focused link I SEE the screen it names load, and the window keep the keyboard focus.
WHEN the link names no screen the kernel has I SEE a refusal in words, and the screen shown stays.
The link is drawn in the accent color on the ground, a pair the palettes hold to the text floor, and underlined when focused, so it is not told by color alone.
WHEN I Tab to the link with VoiceOver (macOS), Narrator (Windows) or Orca (Linux) I HEAR its label and I HEAR it identify itself as a link.
WHEN I list the window's links (VoiceOver's Rotor, Narrator's links list, Orca's list of links) I HEAR the link among them by its label.
WHEN I follow the link I HEAR the new screen's level-1 heading, and the focus is in the new screen.

announce.api: AXLink, its label as the AXTitle and its target as the AXURL (AccessKit Role::Link with its label and URL); AXPress follows it.
ControlType Hyperlink, its label as the Name, its target as the Value, IsKeyboardFocusable; the Invoke pattern follows it.
ATSPI_ROLE_LINK, its label as the name, STATE_FOCUSABLE; the Hyperlink interface gives its URI and the Action interface's jump follows it.

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit, NSAccessibility, UI Automation or AT-SPI provider), so every HEAR check is blocked by the toolkit, and so are the system text size, the platform's high contrast and a magnifier following focus, which it does not report. GPUI's main branch has AccessKit (zed-industries/zed#56065), not yet released (gpui/README.md, "Accessibility tree"). No CI job runs the window tests that show the SEE checks; they run by hand (ACCESSIBILITY.md).
